task: Login Authentication: Session vs JWT vs Refresh Token
hallucination_risk: LOW-MODERATE — core JWT patterns confirmed; @fastify/jwt specifics from general knowledge
UNSURE_resolved: Refresh token storage: SHA-256 hash in DB is standard practice (confirmed by sources)
httpOnly cookie for refresh token is recommended over localStorage (confirmed)
Token rotation + reuse detection is best practice (confirmed)
argon2 preferred for new projects; bcrypt acceptable for existing (confirmed)
@fastify/jwt refresh workflow: custom DB logic needed, not built-in (general knowledge confirmed)

minimal_test: Valid login → access token + refresh cookie set
Valid refresh → new access token + rotated refresh cookie
Reuse revoked refresh → entire family revoked, 401
Expired access but valid refresh → can refresh
CSRF: cross-origin POST /refresh without proper Origin → rejected
rejected_alternatives: Session-based (Redis store) — adds infrastructure dependency, not ideal for stateless REST API
JWT-only no refresh — poor UX, forces frequent re-login
Refresh token in localStorage — XSS vulnerable, confirmed bad practice across sources
OAuth2/OIDC full flow — overkill for single admin dashboard, but viable for multi-service
Access token in cookie only — complicates mobile/non-browser clients
dependency_choice: bcrypt (still safe, widely supported) or argon2 (newer, preferred for new projects per OWASP)
refresh_tokens DB table: id, user_id, token_hash, family_id, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at
implementation_plan: 1. POST /login: bcrypt.compare credentials → issue { accessToken (15min), refreshToken (7d httpOnly cookie) }
2. POST /refresh: read refreshToken from cookie, validate hash in DB, rotate (new refresh + revoke old family or single), issue new access token
3. POST /logout: revoke refresh token in DB, clear cookie
4. Middleware: fastify.addHook('onRequest', async (req, reply) => { await req.jwtVerify() })
5. Token family: on refresh, either rotate entire family (safer) or single token
6. Reuse detection: if a revoked refresh token is presented, revoke entire family (stolen token detection)

Java-focused JWT results dominated; Node.js/Fastify specifics from general knowledge

design_plan.adopted_approach: JWT access token (15min, Bearer header) + refresh token (7d, httpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie) with rotation and reuse detection
key_source_backed_items: Tencent Cloud dev articles confirm JWT refresh token best practice: short-lived access + long-lived refresh
Cookie httpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Strict is standard recommendation
Token rotation + reuse detection is industry standard for refresh tokens
bcrypt still widely recommended; argon2 preferred for new projects per OWASP
risk_list: httpOnly cookie prevents XSS but CSRF still possible without SameSite
Token family rotation adds complexity — need careful transaction handling
Refresh token hash storage: use SHA-256, not raw token
bcrypt vs argon2: both acceptable, argon2 preferred per OWASP 2025 but bcrypt still widely used
JWT signing secret rotation: needs key versioning for zero-downtime rotation
